media_work.title: True Justice: Bryan Stevenson's Fight for Equality
media_work.focus_or_theme: Work of lawyer Bryan Stevenson and the Equal Justice Initiative (EJI), racial injustice in the US legal system, death penalty litigation, wrongful convictions.
media_work.summaryNotes: Highlights EJI's work challenging excessive punishment and racial bias.

media_item.item_title: True Justice: Bryan Stevenson's Fight for Equality
media_item.focus_or_theme: Work of lawyer Bryan Stevenson and the Equal Justice Initiative (EJI), racial injustice in the US legal system, death penalty litigation, wrongful convictions.
media_item.summary_notes: Profiles Bryan Stevenson and EJI's mission, likely using several cases EJI handled, with Walter McMillian's case being a cornerstone example of their work fighting wrongful convictions on death row in the racially biased Southern justice system. The film contextualizes individual cases within the broader history of racial inequality in America.

featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Wrongfully convicted of murder and sentenced to death. He served approximately 6 years on death row before being exonerated when his conviction was overturned, and charges were dropped. His case highlights racial bias and police/prosecutorial misconduct.
contributing_factors_raw: police/prosecutorial misconduct (suppressed evidence, coerced false testimony)
